claims.assertion: The trip is RydeTAXI and metered, so excess kilometres are billed to the rider: $7.46 of the $40.74 total is excess-distance billing (5.29 km × $1.4098/km).

The GPS track shows two off-route segments: 18:17–18:23 adding 2.98 km (up to 1705 m off the optimal route) and 18:26–18:31 adding 1.70 km (up to 1416 m off), totalling 4.68 km of unexplained extra distance against an overall +5.3 km (+37%) over the optimal route.

The first segment (18:17–18:23) is covered by the rider's own consent: the driver asked at 18:12 whether he could go round via Lower Delta Road and the rider replied at 18:13 'Sure, no problem' — both timestamps precede the segment's 18:17 start, and the named-road authorisation is the only route the rider agreed to.

The second segment (18:26–18:31) began 14 minutes after the rider's single consent message of 18:13 and no later message from the rider approves it, so it is not covered by the 'Sure, no problem' reply; it is an unexempted off-route segment.

The driver's post-trip statement that he asked about the jam and that 'the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting' is a claim about his own rerouting, not rider consent, and the rider sent no message authorising that second deviation.

The driver cannot justify the second deviation on congestion grounds because RD-4 requires a traffic record: no incident was recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed bands (Ayer Rajah Expressway band 5 at 40–49 km/h, Central Expressway band 4 at 30–39 km/h) are neither band 1 nor band 2 and therefore at most corroborative, not a standalone exemption.

The refund on the unexempted segment is 1.70 km × $1.4098/km (this trip's distance fare ÷ distance km, per F5) = $2.40, rounded to the cent; only mileage units are refundable and the waiting amount ($0.11, non-metered stop time) is not part of this claim.

The driver has 1 dispute in the last 90 days with 0 upheld, so the RD-6 repeated-violation threshold (a prior upheld route dispute within 90 days) is not met and no account flag should be sought on this record.

weaknesses: The first off-route segment (F3, 2.98 km) is the larger deviation and is expressly consented to by the rider at 18:13 (F10) after the driver's 18:12 request (F9), so RD-5 bars any refund for it; the contestable amount is only 1.70 km.

The consent message is a named-road authorisation ('via Lower Delta Road'): there is no fact tying either driven segment to Lower Delta Road, so on RD-5/G13 the judge may find the scope of the consent covering the first segment undetermined — and, if the case is read that way, the judge could equally treat the pairing of consent with segments as unproven and send the matter to a human instead of awarding the $2.40.

The driver's statement (F12) will be used to argue the second deviation was automatic GPS rerouting rather than a deliberate detour, and the mild congestion bands (F13, F14) will be offered as background justification for it.
The rider's own 90-day record shows 1 dispute, 0 upheld (F17), which the other side may cite on credibility, although it carries no weight under RD-6 by itself.
